chapter: Radio color line, San Francisco and Columbia staff
title: First day on staff at Columbia: five timpani for an Ann Miller picture
summary: His first Columbia picture required him to play melodic timpani parts, so he arrived early to study the music.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: And so we had one out there, anyway, so I was there, and I worked on -- the first picture, I remember very well, the first picture we did there was with Ann Miller. I was trying to think of the title of it, but my first day there, I have to play 5 timpanies. They had written a part that the timpany had the melody, and the whole thing was built around the timpanies, you know, but I told you before about my extreme cockiness, and I was a stickler for getting places on time.

And being a percussionist, if the call was 9 o'clock, I would be there at 8 o'clock, and so being my first day, I was a little apprehensive, and wondering what I was gonna have to play. So I imagine I got there about an hour and a half ahead of time, and so I got there early enough to look at this book and see these timpany parts, you know, really hard!
Had you had any experience playing timpany?
